prompt: Company profile: Aerospace coatings and surface-treatment shop in Savannah, Georgia; 70 employees. The shop has been a small quantity generator (SQG) of hazardous waste (spent solvents, paint waste), historically generating about 600 kg/month. Situation: A new defense contract will roughly triple throughput; projected hazardous waste generation is about 1,400 kg/month on a sustained basis starting next quarter. Georgia's EPD administers an authorized RCRA program. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
**Compliance Obligations Register – Aerospace Coatings Shop (Savannah, GA)** **Generator Status Change: SQG → LQG (600 kg/month → 1,400 kg/month)** --- ### **Obligation 1: Notification of Generator Status Change to Regulatory Authority** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Submit written notification to Georgia EPD within 30 days of first exceeding 1,000 kg/month hazardous waste generation threshold, indicating change from SQG to LQG status. Must obtain EPA ID Number if not already assigned. | | **Source** | 40 CFR 262.18(a); Georgia Rules for Hazardous Waste Management (391-3-11-.05(2)); Georgia EPD Hazardous Waste Management Branch notification procedures | | **Applicability** | Directly applicable upon sustained generation >1,000 kg/month. Company projects 1,400 kg/month starting next quarter, triggering LQG requirements. Defense contract provides long-term certainty of status change. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Maps directly** – Environmental compliance obligation; change in legal status creates new legal requirements for waste management controls. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Maps directly** – OHS legal requirement; increased hazardous materials and waste handling creates new employee exposure risks requiring additional controls. | | **Evaluation Method & Frequency (9.1.2)** | **How:** Review of Georgia EPD acknowledgment letter, EPA ID number confirmation, and internal waste generation tracking records.
**When:** (1) Within 30 days of status change; (2) Quarterly review of waste generation logs to confirm sustained LQG status; (3) Annual compliance audit. | --- ### **Obligation 2: 90-Day Accumulation Time Limit for Hazardous Waste** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | LQGs may accumulate hazardous waste on-site for a maximum of 90 days without obtaining a storage permit. Must mark containers with "Hazardous Waste" and accumulation start date. | | **Source** | 40 CFR 262.17(a); 40 CFR 262.34(a); Georgia Rule 391-3-11-.05(2)(a) | | **Applicability** | Critical operational constraint. Current SQG 180-day limit no longer applies. Tripled waste volume increases risk of exceeding 90-day limit without enhanced inventory management. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Maps directly** – Environmental operational control requirement; prevents unpermitted storage and potential releases. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Maps indirectly** – Supports OHS risk control by limiting on-site hazardous material quantities and exposure duration. | | **Evaluation Method & Frequency (9.1.2)** | **How:** Weekly visual inspections of waste accumulation areas; monthly reconciliation of waste generation logs vs. shipment manifests; quarterly internal audit of container labeling and dates.
**When:** (1) Continuous during operations; (2) Monthly compliance checks; (3) Quarterly audit; (4) Immediately upon any shipment delay notification. | --- ### **Obligation 3: Contingency Plan & Emergency Procedures** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Develop, maintain, and implement a written contingency plan to minimize hazards from fires, explosions, or unplanned releases. Must include emergency coordinator, emergency equipment list, and coordination with local emergency responders. Plan must be kept on-site and reviewed annually. | | **Source** | 40 CFR 262.34(a)(4); 40 CFR 262.34(d)(5)(vi); Georgia Rule 391-3-11-.05(2)(a)4 | | **Applicability** | Mandatory for LQGs. Increased waste volumes and defense contract complexity elevate spill/release risks. Savannah Fire Department and Chatham County EMA coordination required. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Maps directly** – Environmental emergency preparedness and response legal requirement. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Maps directly** – OHS legal requirement for emergency response planning; addresses employee safety during hazardous waste incidents. | | **Evaluation Method & Frequency (9.1.2)** | **How:** Annual review and update of plan; annual emergency response drill with documentation; quarterly inspection of emergency equipment; verification of emergency coordinator training records.
**When:** (1) Within 90 days of LQG status; (2) Annually thereafter; (3) Within 24 hours of any emergency incident; (4) When operations or waste types change. | --- ### **Obligation 4: Personnel Training for Hazardous Waste Management** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Ensure all personnel who handle hazardous waste or emergency response receive initial training within 6 months of hire/assignment and annual refresher training. Maintain training records for 3 years. | | **Source** | 40 CFR 265.16; Georgia Rule 391-3-11-.05(2)(a)5 | | **Applicability** | Applies to all 70 employees in waste-generating operations (paint booths, surface treatment, waste handlers). New defense contract may introduce new waste streams requiring additional training. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Maps indirectly** – Supports environmental competence requirement (7.2) but is a direct legal compliance obligation. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Maps directly** – OHS legal requirement for worker competency on hazardous materials handling and emergency procedures. | | **Evaluation Method & Frequency (9.1.2)** | **How:** Review training records for completion and content adequacy; employee interviews; observation of waste handling practices; post-training assessments.
**When:** (1) Within 6 months of new employee assignment; (2) Annually for refresher training; (3) Quarterly spot-checks; (4) After any process change or incident. | --- ### **Obligation 5: Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest System** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Use EPA Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest (Form 8700-22) for all off-site shipments. Must retain copy for 3 years. Generator must certify waste is properly packaged, labeled, and marked. | | **Source** | 40 CFR 262.20-23; Georgia Rule 391-3-11-.05(2)(b) | | **Applicability** | All LQG waste shipments require manifests. Increased shipment frequency from tripled volume raises documentation burden. Must register with EPA e-Manifest system. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Maps directly** – Environmental legal requirement for waste tracking and verification of proper disposal. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Maps indirectly** – Ensures transporter safety and proper handling, reducing downstream OHS risks. | | **Evaluation Method & Frequency (9.1.2)** | **How:** Monthly reconciliation of manifests with waste shipment records; quarterly audit of manifest completeness; annual verification of transporter/TSDF EPA IDs.
**When:** (1) For each shipment; (2) Monthly; (3) Quarterly audit; (4) Within 30 days of receiving signed manifest copy from TSDF. | --- ### **Obligation 6: Biennial Hazardous Waste Report** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Submit biennial report (due March 1 of even-numbered years) detailing types, quantities, and disposition of hazardous waste generated during previous year. | | **Source** | 40 CFR 262.41; Georgia Rule 391-3-11-.05(2)(c) | | **Applicability** | Mandatory for LQGs. First report due March 1, 2026 (for 2025 data) if LQG status achieved in Q1 2025. Defense contract waste must be separately tracked. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Maps directly** – Environmental reporting legal requirement. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Maps indirectly** – Waste characterization data supports OHS risk assessment for employee exposures. | | **Evaluation Method & Frequency (9.1.2)** | **How:** Internal data validation against manifest and production records; third-party review of report before submission; verification of state acknowledgment.
**When:** (1) Data compilation quarterly to ensure accuracy; (2) Final review in January of reporting year; (3) Submission by March 1 deadline; (4) Annual audit of data collection process. | --- ### **Obligation 7: Pre-Transport Requirements (Packaging, Labeling, Marking, Placarding)** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Package waste in DOT-compliant containers, mark with proper shipping name/ID number, label with hazard class, and placard vehicles per 49 CFR. Must comply with both RCRA and DOT regulations. | | **Source** | 40 CFR 262.30-32; 49 CFR Parts 172-178; Georgia Rule 391-3-11-.05(2)(b) | | **Applicability** | All off-site shipments. Increased volume and defense contract security requirements may necessitate specialized packaging/labeling protocols. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Maps directly** – Environmental legal requirement preventing releases during transport. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Maps directly** – OHS legal requirement protecting employees who package/load waste and transport personnel. | | **Evaluation Method & Frequency (9.1.2)** | **How:** Pre-shipment inspections; quarterly audit of packaging supplies and procedures; employee competency verification; review of DOT training records.
**When:** (1) Before each waste shipment; (2) Quarterly; (3) After any packaging supplier change; (4) Annually for DOT refresher training verification. | --- ### **Obligation 8: Georgia State-Specific Fees and Reporting** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Register as LQG with Georgia EPD and pay annual hazardous waste generator fees ($1,000-$5,000 based on volume). Submit annual generator survey and maintain state-specific waste reduction plan. | | **Source** | Georgia Hazardous Waste Management Act (O.C.G.A. §12-8-60 et seq.); Georgia Rule 391-3-11-.06; Georgia EPD Fee Schedule | | **Applicability** | Georgia-specific requirement. Fee obligation begins upon LQG status. Savannah facility must coordinate with Georgia EPD District Office. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Maps directly** – State environmental compliance obligation. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Does not map** – Purely environmental regulatory fee/reporting. | | **Evaluation Method & Frequency (9.1.2)** | **How:** Review of fee payment receipts; verification of annual survey submission; audit of waste reduction plan implementation.
**When:** (1) Annually by July 1 (fee payment); (2) Annually by March 31 (generator survey); (3) Quarterly review of waste reduction metrics; (4) During annual compliance audit. | --- ### **Obligation 9: Air Emissions from Waste Management (NESHAP/Title V Implications)** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Increased waste generation may trigger review of air emissions from waste storage areas. If waste contains VOCs/HAPs, may need to update Title V permit or NESHAP compliance demonstration for Subpart TTTT (Surface Coating). | | **Source** | 40 CFR 63 Subpart TTTT; Georgia Rule 391-3-1-.02 (Title V Operating Permits) | | **Applicability** | Indirect but critical. Tripled throughput increases both coating usage and waste generation. Must evaluate if waste storage VOC emissions exceed de minimis thresholds or if Title V permit modification required. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Maps directly** – Environmental air quality compliance obligation. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Maps indirectly** – Air emissions affect employee chemical exposure (industrial hygiene). | | **Evaluation Method & Frequency (9.1.2)** | **How:** Air emissions inventory update; modeling of waste storage area emissions; consultation with Georgia EPD Air Protection Branch; permit applicability analysis.
**When:** (1) Within 60 days of new operational levels; (2) Annually with Title V compliance certification; (3) When waste composition changes; (4) During triennial Title V permit review. | --- ### **Obligation 10: Process Safety Management (PSM) Threshold Evaluation** | **Element** | **Details** | |-------------|-------------| | **Requirement** | Evaluate if increased quantities of flammable liquids (solvents) in waste/process trigger OSHA PSM standard (29 CFR 1910.119) threshold of 10,000 lbs of flammable liquids in process. | | **Source** | 29 CFR 1910.119(a)(1)(ii); 29 CFR 1910.119(b) | | **Applicability** | Must assess if combined on-site inventory of flammable solvents (in process + waste accumulation) exceeds 10,000 lbs. Defense contract may increase both simultaneously. | | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** | **Does not map** – Purely OHS safety management. | | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** | **Maps directly** – OHS legal requirement for process safety if threshold exceeded. | | **Evaluation Method & Frequency (9.1.2)** | **How:** Calculate maximum on-site flammable liquid inventory (process tanks + waste containers); compare to PSM threshold; document assessment.
**When:** (1) Immediately upon achieving new production levels; (2) Quarterly inventory reviews; (3) Whenever new solvent types introduced; (4) Annually as part of OHS risk assessment. | --- ### **Summary Compliance Evaluation Schedule (ISO 9.1.2)** | **Obligation** | **Continuous** | **Monthly** | **Quarterly** | **Annual** | **Event-Triggered** | |----------------|----------------|-------------|---------------|------------|---------------------| | Generator Status Notification | | | | | ✓ (30 days) | | 90-Day Accumulation | ✓ (weekly) | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ (delays) | | Contingency Plan | | | | ✓ | ✓ (incidents/ops changes) | | Personnel Training | | | ✓ (spot checks) | ✓ | ✓ (new hires/process changes) | | Manifest System | ✓ (per shipment) | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ (TSDF returns) | | Biennial Report | | | | ✓ (odd years) | | | Pre-Transport | ✓ (per shipment) | | ✓ | ✓ (DOT training) | ✓ (supplier changes) | | Georgia Fees/Reporting | | | | ✓ | | | Air Emissions | | | | ✓ | ✓ (new levels) | | PSM Evaluation | | | | ✓ | ✓ (inventory changes) | **Note:** All obligations should be evaluated during the annual internal audit cycle per ISO 9.1.2, with frequency adjusted based on risk and performance.
